ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The top of the figure is the +10 V power supply node; on the left there is a 10 kΩ resistor connected from +10 V to the transistor base; on the right there is a 50 kΩ resistor connected from +10 V to the transistor collector; the transistor emitter is connected downward through a 100 Ω resistor to ground, and the output V0 is marked at the node of the emitter and the upper end of the 100 Ω resistor. Reasoning: According to the problem statement and the specified method, let the emitter voltage VE = V0. For the silicon transistor VBE = 0.7 V, so the base voltage VB = V0 + 0.7. The 10 kΩ resistor current is the base current: IB = [10 - (V0 + 0.7)] / 10000 = (9.3 - V0) / 10000. The emitter current IE = V0 / 100. method.method_draft: First identify from the image that V0 is the emitter voltage across the 100 Ω resistor, and the base is driven from +10 V through 10 kΩ. Let V_E = V0, so V_B = V0 + 0.7.
